title: Veltrix Motors adds a third shift at Chakan as Tarang SUV bookings cross 40,000
body: Veltrix Motors will add a third production shift at its Chakan plant after bookings for the Tarang mid-size SUV crossed 40,000 in the first seven weeks. The capacity expansion lifts monthly output from 7,000 to 11,500 units by December and will require an additional 18,000 tyres a month across the 17-inch and 18-inch fitments. The company said it is qualifying a second tyre supplier for the top-end variants to de-risk supply during the festive season and has asked vendors to submit quotations for original equipment and replacement-market kits by the end of September. Analysts expect the Tarang to take a double-digit share of the mid-size SUV segment within a year, and dealers report waiting periods of up to ten weeks for the top variants.

title: Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles wins order for 2,400 diesel and CNG buses from three state transport undertakings
body: Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles has been awarded an order for 2,400 buses from three state transport undertakings in Karnataka, Telangana and Odisha, its largest single order this decade. The fleet mix includes 1,600 CNG city buses and 800 diesel intercity coaches, with deliveries scheduled between January and October 2027. Bharatrath said the tender specified radial tyres with a guaranteed retreadable casing life, and it is negotiating a fleet tyre management contract that bundles fitment, pressure monitoring and retreading at the operators' depots. Industry observers said the order is one of the largest public bus procurements this year and will keep Bharatrath's Hosur and Lucknow plants running at near full capacity through 2027.

title: Cabzy Mobility to refresh 6,000 ride-hailing cars with electric sedans across five metros
body: Cabzy Mobility will replace 6,000 ageing petrol cars in its owned fleet with electric sedans over the next twelve months, starting with Delhi and Bengaluru in November. The ride-hailing company said the refresh is backed by a leasing facility from two non-bank lenders and will cut its per-kilometre operating cost by nearly a third. Cabzy is inviting proposals for a pay-per-kilometre tyre programme for the new fleet, including low rolling resistance tyres, puncture support and monthly tread audits at its 22 charging hubs. Cabzy said drivers will be offered the new electric sedans on a lease-to-own plan, and the company expects the fleet refresh to add 4,000 driver partners by the end of the year.

title: Kavero Electric raises USD 120 million Series C to build a second electric SUV line in Hosur
body: Kavero Electric has raised USD 120 million in a Series C round to fund a second assembly line at its Hosur plant and the launch of a seven-seat electric SUV in 2027. The new line doubles annual capacity to 90,000 vehicles. Kavero's chief operating officer said the company will localise wheels, tyres and thermal components for the new model and expects to nominate suppliers by the end of the year. The round was led by a climate-focused growth fund, with participation from existing investors. The company delivered 38,000 vehicles in the last financial year and said the new SUV is already being tested in hot-weather trials in Rajasthan ahead of homologation next summer.

title: Nirvaan Motors breaks ground on INR 4,800 crore passenger vehicle plant in Dharwad
body: Nirvaan Motors has broken ground on a new passenger vehicle plant near Dharwad with an investment of INR 4,800 crore and an initial capacity of 150,000 vehicles a year. The first phase, due in mid-2028, will build a compact SUV and a small electric hatchback on a shared platform. The company said it intends to source more than 90 per cent of parts from suppliers within 300 kilometres of the site and will open vendor registration for tyres, glass and seating systems in October. The state government has committed road connectivity and a dedicated power substation for the site, and the company expects the plant to create about 6,500 direct jobs over five years.

title: Tezrun Two Wheelers launches 125cc commuter scooter, targets 25,000 units a month
body: Tezrun Two Wheelers has launched the Zippa, a 125cc commuter scooter built at its Hosur facility, with a production target of 25,000 units a month by March. The company is expanding its dealer network from 600 to 900 outlets across tier-two and tier-three towns. Tezrun said the scooter uses 12-inch tubeless tyres on both wheels and that it is adding a second tyre vendor to support the volume ramp-up and a planned export programme to Nepal and Bangladesh next year. Tezrun sold 190,000 scooters and motorcycles last year and said the new model is its first to be designed entirely at its Chennai engineering centre, with a warranty of five years.

title: Haulmark Freight raises Series B funding to add 1,500 heavy trucks to its long-haul fleet
body: Digital trucking operator Haulmark Freight has raised INR 650 crore in a Series B round and will use the capital to add 1,500 heavy trucks to its owned long-haul fleet over the next 18 months. The company runs dedicated lanes for FMCG and cement customers between Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata. Haulmark said tyres are its second-largest operating cost after fuel, and it is evaluating fleet tyre partners that offer telematics-based pressure monitoring, scheduled rotation and a guaranteed cost per kilometre. Haulmark currently operates 2,300 trucks, of which about 900 are owned, and the new vehicles will be deployed on contracted lanes with minimum volume guarantees from anchor customers.

title: Saarthi eBus awarded tender to supply and operate 900 electric buses in Hyderabad
body: Saarthi eBus has been awarded a gross-cost-contract tender to supply and operate 900 electric buses for Hyderabad's city transport authority for twelve years. Deliveries begin in April 2027 from the company's new assembly plant at Zaheerabad. The contract makes Saarthi responsible for maintenance, including tyres, for the life of the fleet, and the company said it will sign long-term supply and retreading agreements for low-floor city bus tyres before the first batch is delivered. The operator expects the buses to run about 220 kilometres a day each, and the transport authority has linked a part of monthly payments to fleet availability and on-time performance.

title: QuickHop expands electric scooter rental fleet to 20,000 vehicles in eight cities
body: Micro-mobility start-up QuickHop will expand its electric scooter rental fleet from 7,000 to 20,000 vehicles across eight cities by the end of the financial year, after closing a debt round with two banks. The scooters are used mainly by delivery riders on weekly rental plans. QuickHop said it is standardising on puncture-resistant tubeless tyres and wants a supplier that can run doorstep tyre replacement at its 60 swap-and-service points. QuickHop said average utilisation across its fleet is above 85 per cent, and that tyre punctures are currently the most common reason for unplanned vehicle downtime in its busiest cities.

title: Ashvik Motors launches electric intermediate truck, opens order books with 1,100 units
body: Ashvik Motors has launched a 14-tonne electric intermediate commercial truck aimed at cement, e-commerce and port logistics operators, and says it already holds orders for 1,100 units. Production starts at its Pithampur plant in January with a capacity of 6,000 trucks a year. The company is finalising tyre fitments for the regenerative braking drive axle and has invited leading tyre makers to run joint durability trials on the Indore-Mumbai corridor. Ashvik said early customers include two cement makers and a port logistics operator, and that it expects electric trucks to make up a quarter of its volumes by the end of 2028.

title: Dunecrest Logistics orders 700 prime movers for Gulf cross-border freight corridor
body: Dunecrest Logistics has placed an order for 700 prime movers and 1,200 trailers to expand its cross-border freight service between Jebel Ali, Riyadh and Muscat. The fleet expansion is financed by a USD 95 million facility and is timed with the opening of a new customs corridor next year. Dunecrest said high desert temperatures make tyre performance critical, and it will tender a five-year contract for heat-resistant truck tyres, retreading and roadside assistance across the network. The company said it expects cross-border freight volumes in the region to grow by about 12 per cent a year, driven by new manufacturing zones and rising e-commerce shipments.

title: Khanij Earthworks adds 180 dumpers and loaders for new iron ore mining contract in Odisha
body: Khanij Earthworks has won a seven-year mining services contract at an iron ore block in Keonjhar and will add 180 rigid dump trucks, wheel loaders and graders to its fleet. The equipment order is valued at about INR 1,100 crore. Khanij said off-the-road tyres are the most supply-constrained item in its expansion plan and that it is looking for a partner to provide OTR tyres with on-site monitoring, rotation and repair at the mine. Khanij currently operates more than 600 pieces of heavy equipment across limestone, coal and iron ore mines, and expects revenue from the new contract to begin in the next quarter.
